questions.q: Determine the unit digit of $98^{99^{100^{101}}}$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Base $8$ hai, toh cyclicity $4$ ki lagegi. Power dekh ke ghabrana nahi, sirf parity (odd/even) ka game hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Power ko $4$ se divide karo: $99 \pmod 4 = 3 \equiv -1$.
Ab is $99$ ke upar ki power dekho: $100^{101}$, jo ki definitely ek EVEN number hai.
$(-1)^{\text{Even}} = +1$. Matlab reduced effective power $1$ ho gayi.
Unit digit = $8^1 = 8$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Power of power (ladder exponent) me humesha base of ladder ko mod cyclicity karte hain. Phir uske exponent ka nature (odd ya even) check karte hain.

Future Exam Takeaway:
CDS aur SSC aise hi power ladders dete hain time waste karne ke liye. Modulo $4$ aur Odd/Even nature se ye $5$ second me break hota hai.

questions.q: When a number is successively divided by $3, 4$ and $7$, the remainders obtained are $2, 3$ and $5$, respectively. What will be the remainder when $84$ divides the same number?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Successive division ka fixed structure hota hai. Sabse chhota number nikal ke direct $84$ (jo ki $3 \times 4 \times 7$ hai) se divide kar do.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Table method reverse me lagao, let final quotient be $0$.
Step 1: $(7 \times 0) + 5 = 5$.
Step 2: $(4 \times 5) + 3 = 23$.
Step 3: $(3 \times 23) + 2 = 71$.
Smallest number mil gaya $71$.
Ab $71$ ko $84$ se divide karo, remainder $71$ hi bachega!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Yahan divisors ka product $3 \times 4 \times 7 = 84$ hai. Jab bhi same product se final divide karne ko bole, toh jo original smallest number aata hai, wahi directly remainder hota hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Always assume the last quotient as $0$ to find the absolute minimum number. This prevents calculation errors and saves time.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $36363636$ is divided by $101$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Ek dam free ke marks! $2$-digit number ki repeating sequence hamesha $101$ se judti hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Any number of the form $abab$ is completely divisible by $101$ ($ab \times 101$).
Yahan $36363636$ extended form hai, jo strictly $36360000 + 3636$ ki sequence se banta hai.
Chunki ye completely multiple hai, Remainder = $0$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Format $xyxy = xy \times 101$. $abababab$ ka format essentially $ab \times 1010101$ hai. Yahan pair perfectly $101$ ka multiple banata hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Pattern $xyxy$ is div by $101$. $xyzxyz$ is div by $1001$. Memorize these structural primes.

questions.q: A printer numbers the pages of a book starting with $1$ and uses $5189$ digits in all. How many pages does the book have?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Page numbering ke digit chunks yaad hone chahiye. $999$ pages tak $2889$ digits hote hain. Uske upar sab $4$-digit wale hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Pages $1$ to $999$ use exactly $2889$ digits.
Remaining digits = $5189 - 2889 = 2300$ digits.
Ye saare bachhe hue digits $4$-digit number banayenge.
Number of $4$-digit pages = $2300 \div 4 = 575$ pages.
Total pages = $999 + 575 = 1574$ pages.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Breakdown: $1-9$ ($9$ digits), $10-99$ ($180$ digits), $100-999$ ($2700$ digits). Total = $2889$. Ye sequence yaad rakhne se time bachta hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Always memorize standard digit counts: $1$ to $99 = 189$ digits. $1$ to $999 = 2889$ digits. Direct application se calculation aadhi ho jati hai.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $2^{100}$ is divided by $102$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Base $2$ aur Divisor $102$ coprime nahi hain. Iska matlab direct totient nahi lagega, pehle 'Cancellation Rule' lagana padega!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Expression: $\frac{2^{100}}{102} = \frac{2 \times 2^{99}}{2 \times 51}$. Upar niche $2$ se cancel kar do. Nayi form: $\frac{2^{99}}{51}$.
Euler's Totient $\phi(51) = 51 \times \left(1 - \frac{1}{3}\right) \times \left(1 - \frac{1}{17}\right) = 32$.
Power reduce: $99 \pmod{32} = 3$.
Remainder of $\frac{2^3}{51} = \frac{8}{51}$ is $8$.
Crucial Step: Jis $2$ se pehle kata tha, usko wapis multiply karo! $8 \times 2 = 16$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Agar $\text{HCF}(a, n) > 1$ ho, toh Euler ya Fermat fail ho jate hain. Pehle common factor HCF cancel karke coprime banao, solve karo, aur end me HCF se wapas multiply karo.

Future Exam Takeaway:
SSC CGL Mains me cancellation rule ka ye trap bohot common hai. Cancellation factor ko side me likh liya karo taaki end me bhool na jao.

questions.q: If a number $54k31m82$ is divisible by $11$, what will be the maximum value of $(k+m)$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Divisibility of $11$ calls for the difference of alternate sums. 'Maximum value' pucha hai matlab variables ki badi digits test karni padengi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Sum of odd places: $2 + m + 3 + 4 = 9 + m$.
Sum of even places: $8 + 1 + k + 5 = 14 + k$.
Difference: $(14 + k) - (9 + m) = 5 + k - m$.
Condition for $11$: Diff must be $0$ or $11$.
Case 1: $5 + k - m = 0 \implies m - k = 5$. Pairs for max sum: $m=9, k=4 \implies$ Sum = $13$.
Case 2: $5 + k - m = 11 \implies k - m = 6$. Pairs for max sum: $k=9, m=3 \implies$ Sum = $12$.
Maximum of both cases is $13$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Single digits me maximum limit $9$ hoti hai. Equation me badi limit push karne ke liye $9$ ko explicitly rakh ke check karna hi best strategy hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Humesha dono cases ($0$ aur $11$) check karo, kyunki Examiner randomly max value kisi ek case me shift kar deta hai.

questions.q: Find the last two digits of $19^{19^{19}}$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Base ends in $9$. Aakhiri do digits nikalne hain, matlab $\pmod{100}$ karna hai. Yahan cyclicity of tens place lagani hogi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
$19^2 = 361 \equiv 61 \pmod{100}$. Cyclicity of bases ending in $9$ modulo $100$ is usually $10$.
Calculate effective power $19^{19} \pmod{10}$: $19 \equiv -1 \pmod{10} \implies (-1)^{19} = -1 \equiv 9 \pmod{10}$.
So we need last two digits of $19^9$.
$19^9 = 19 \times (19^2)^4 = 19 \times (61)^4$.
Shortcut for $61^4$: unit is $1$, tens is $6 \times 4 = 24 \implies 4$. Last two = $41$.
$19 \times 41 = 779 \implies 79$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
For any number ending in $1$, $(x1)^y$, the last two digits are $(\text{unit digit of } x \times y)1$. Isliye $61^4 \implies (6\times4)1 = 41$ aaya.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Whenever asked for last two digits of numbers ending in $3, 7,$ or $9$, always raise them to a power that ends in $1$ (like $19^2=361$) and then apply the $x1$ binomial shortcut.

questions.q: A number consists of two digits and the digit in the ten's place exceeds that in the unit's place by $5$. If $5$ times the sum of the digits is subtracted from the number, the digits of the number are reversed. Then the sum of the digits of the number is:
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Basic number system property: $(N - \text{Reverse of } N) = 9(x-y)$. Direct equation put karni hai, no lengthy algebra.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Given: Tens digit exceeds units by $5 \implies x - y = 5$.
Standard Rule: $N - \text{Reverse} = 9(x-y) = 9(5) = 45$.
Question says: $N - 5(x+y) = \text{Reverse} \implies N - \text{Reverse} = 5(x+y)$.
Equating both: $5(x+y) = 45 \implies x+y = 9$.
Bhai sum directly $9$ aa gaya, number was $72$. Options dekhte hi khatam!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Agar details verify karni ho: $x-y=5$ aur $x+y=9$. Solve kiya toh $x=7, y=2$. Number $72$ ban gaya. Reverse $27$. $72 - 27 = 45$. Condition satisfied.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Difference between a $2$-digit number and its reverse is ALWAYS $9(x-y)$. Sum is ALWAYS $11(x+y)$. Isko muh-zubaani yaad rakho.

questions.q: Find the smallest number which is perfectly divisible by $7$, but when divided by $6, 9,$ and $15$ leaves a remainder of $4$ in each case.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Number $7$ se divisible hona chahiye. Options check karo! $94, 184, 544$ $7$ se nahi katte. Sirf $364$ kat raha hai. Exam me solve karna hi nahi tha!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Maths approach: $\text{LCM}$ of $6, 9, 15 = 90$.
Number is of the form $90k + 4$.
Condition: $(90k + 4)$ is divisible by $7$.
Find remainder of $90/7 \implies 6$. So, $(6k + 4)$ must be div by $7$.
Put $k=4 \implies 6(4)+4 = 28$ (divisible by $7$).
Original Number $= 90(4) + 4 = 364$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
We reduce $90k \pmod 7$ to make calculation smaller. $90 = 12 \times 7 + 6$. Hamesha remainder equation bana ke minimum $k$ dhoondo.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Aise sawalo me sabse pehle divisibility rule lagao options par. $90\%$ cases me $1$ hi option match karega aur $5$ seconds me mark karke aage badh jaoge!

questions.q: What is the remainder when $18!$ is divided by $23$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Factorial division by prime! Ye seedha Wilson's Theorem ka derivative hai. Wilson kehta hai $(P-1)! \equiv -1 \pmod P$.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
$23$ prime hai. By Wilson's Theorem: $22! \equiv -1 \pmod{23}$.
Isko $18!$ tak piche khicho:
$22 \times 21 \times 20 \times 19 \times 18! \equiv -1 \pmod{23}$.
Negative remainders apply karo $\pmod{23}$: $(-1)(-2)(-3)(-4) \times 18! \equiv -1$.
$24 \times 18! \equiv -1$.
Now $24 \equiv 1 \pmod{23}$.
So, $1 \times 18! \equiv -1$.
To make remainder positive: $23 - 1 = 22$. Answer $22$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Negative remainders calculation ko extremely short banate hain. $22$ is practically $-1$ w.r.t $23$. Yahi step multiply karne ka dard bachaata hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Agar $(P-x)! \pmod P$ pucha ho toh negative remainders ka back-gear lagao, direct answer niklega.

questions.q: The 6-digit number $537xy5$ is divisible by $125$. How many possible values can the digit $x$ take?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Divisibility by $125$ ($5^3$) means checking ONLY the last $3$ digits. Poora number ignore maaro.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Last $3$ digits hain $xy5$.
$125$ ke $3$-digit multiples ending in $5$ are: $125, 375, 625, 875$.
Yani $x$ ki place pe values ho sakti hain: $1, 3, 6, 8$.
Total possible values for $x$ are exactly $4$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Jaise $8$ ($2^3$) ke liye last $3$ digits dekhte hain, waise hi $125$ ($5^3$) ke liye karte hain. Even endings ($250, 500, 750$) valid nahi the kyunki unit digit fix $5$ hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Remember the standard endings for $125$: $125, 250, 375, 500, 625, 750, 875, 000$. Direct filter out karo given conditions se.

questions.q: Let $ab$ (where $a \ne b$) be a two-digit prime number such that $ba$ is also a prime number. The sum of all such numbers is:
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Bhai $2$-digit primes gine-chune hote hain. Reversible prime pairs toh aur bhi limited hain, bas dimaag me count karna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Find pairs of $(ab, ba)$ which both are primes, and $a \ne b$ (eliminates $11$).
Pairs are: $(13, 31)$, $(17, 71)$, $(37, 73)$, $(79, 97)$.
Total $8$ numbers. Unka sum nikalna hai:
$13+31+17+71+37+73+79+97 = 418$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Baki combination jaise $23$ (rev $32$ is even), $47$ (rev $74$ is even), ya $19$ (rev $91 = 13 \times 7$) trap hote hain. Hamesha reverse ko factorize karne ki aadat dalo.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Reversible primes up to $100$ ko 'Emirp primes' bolte hain. Inka set $\{13, 17, 31, 37, 71, 73, 79, 97\}$ direct yaad hona chahiye.

questions.q: Find the greatest possible 5-digit number of the form $4a3b2$ which is divisible by $36$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
'Greatest' pucha hai matlab hum digits ko $9$ se check karna shuru karenge. Divisibility $36$ yani $4$ and $9$ dono lagana hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Number is $4a3b2$. For divisibility by $4$, last two digits '$b2$' must be divisible.
To maximize, test largest $b$: $b=9 \implies 92$ is div by $4$. So $b=9$ set kar do.
Now number is $4a392$. For divisibility by $9$, digital sum must be div by $9$.
Sum $= 4 + a + 3 + 9 + 2 = 18 + a$.
To maximize, put $a=9 \implies 18+9 = 27$ (div by $9$).
So the greatest number is $49392$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Pehle hamesha choti constraint wala rule lagao (jaise $4$ ke liye bas last $2$ digits). Phir global rule (jaise $9$ ke liye sabka sum) apply karo.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Maximization ke questions me variable ko default $9$ assume karke condition check kiya karo, speed $2x$ ho jayegi.

questions.q: How many integers between $299$ and $501$ are divisible by $4$ or $10$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Venn diagram set theory (Inclusion-Exclusion Principle) ka classic application! Formula $n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B)$ dimag me flash hona chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Numbers between $299$ and $501$ (Total $201$ numbers from $300$ to $500$).
Div by $4$: $300, 304, \dots, 500 \implies \frac{500-300}{4} + 1 = 51$.
Div by $10$: $300, 310, \dots, 500 \implies \frac{500-300}{10} + 1 = 21$.
Div by LCM $20$ (intersection): $300, 320, \dots, 500 \implies \frac{500-300}{20} + 1 = 11$.
Total integers = $51 + 21 - 11 = 61$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Series ki total terms nikalne ka JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) $\implies \frac{\text{Last} - \text{First}}{\text{Common Difference}} + 1$. Isko directly mentally count kiya karo.

Future Exam Takeaway:
'Or' likha ho toh humesha LCM wala part subtract karna hai nahi toh double counting ho jayegi. Ye SSC ka sabse favourite trap hai.

questions.q: If $68A3Y$ is divisible by $3, 7$ and $11$, find $4A+3Y$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Divisibility by $3, 7$, and $11$ means divisible by their LCM, $3 \times 7 \times 11 = 231$.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Assume max possible value $68939$ and divide by $231$.
$68939 \div 231 = 298$ (Quotient) and Remainder = $101$.
Subtract remainder to get perfect multiple: $68939 - 101 = 68838$.
Compare $68838$ with $68A3Y \implies A = 8, Y = 8$.
Value of $4A + 3Y = 4(8) + 3(8) = 32 + 24 = 56$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Alternating sums for $11$ and digital roots for $3$ can also form equations, but LCM subtraction is fool-proof and fastest.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Whenever a number with missing digits is divisible by $7, 11, 13$ or $3, 7, 11$, always pad it with $9$s, find the remainder with LCM, and subtract!

questions.q: If a number $P$ is divided by $D$, the remainder is $14$. When $3P$ is divided by the same divisor $D$, the remainder is $8$. What is the value of the divisor $D$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Agar number $3$ guna ho raha hai, toh mathematically remainder bhi $3$ guna hoga (temporarily). Naya remainder tabhi ghatega jab Divisor se bhaag lagega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Old Remainder was $14$. Condition says number is multiplied by $3$ ($3P$).
Temporary New Remainder $= 14 \times 3 = 42$.
Actual Remainder given is $8$.
Iska seedha matlab hai: $42$ ko jab Divisor $D$ se bhag diya, toh $8$ bacha.
$42 - D = 8 \implies D = 34$. Divisor $34$ hai!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Algebraically: $P = kD + 14$. Then $3P = 3kD + 42$. $3kD$ is fully divisible. Modulo operation pe focus karo: $42 \equiv 8 \pmod D \implies 42 - 8 = 34$, which is a multiple of $D$. $D$ could be $17$ or $34$, options me se $34$ correct hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Operation performed on the number is EXACTLY performed on its remainder. Remainder exceeds divisor? Subtract divisor. Simple!

questions.q: If $n$ is a positive integer, then when $1^{n}+2^{n}+3^{n}+4^{n}$ is divided by $10$, how many possible remainders can there be?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dividing by $10$ is just finding the Unit Digit! We only need to check cycles of powers up to $4$.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Put $n=1$: $1+2+3+4 = 10 \implies$ Unit digit $0$.
Put $n=2$: $1+4+9+6 = 20 \implies$ Unit digit $0$.
Put $n=3$: $1+8+7+4 = 20 \implies$ Unit digit $0$.
Put $n=4$: $1+6+1+6 = 14 \implies$ Unit digit $4$.
Possible remainders are only $0$ and $4$. That means exactly $2$ possible remainders.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
The cyclicity of unit digits for $1, 2, 3, 4$ repeats every $4$th power. So checking $n=1,2,3,4$ covers all infinite possibilities.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Divisibility by $10$ ALWAYS means 'Find the Unit Digit'. Don't waste time thinking about complex polynomial theorems. CGL bas unit digit check karwana chahta hai!

questions.q: What is the remainder when the sum $(10^1 + 10^2 + 10^3 + \dots + 10^{100})$ is divided by $6$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
$10$ aur $6$ ka relation cyclicity me fix hai! $10$ ki koi bhi power ko $6$ se divide karo, remainder hamesha $4$ aayega. Pattern identify kiya toh $2$ second ka sawal hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
$10^1 \pmod 6 = 4$.
$10^2 = 100 \pmod 6 = 4$.
There are $100$ such terms in the series.
Sum of remainders = $4 \times 100 = 400$.
Final step: $400 \pmod 6$. $400 = 396 + 4 \implies$ Remainder $4$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Modular arithmetic me addition distribute ho jata hai. Tum series ko sum kar ke mod lo ya individually mod leke sum karo, answer same aayega. Yahan individual remainder fix hai ($4$) isliye multiply kar diya.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Series based questions hamesha repeating remainders par set hote hain. First $2-3$ terms check karo, pattern apne aap chilla ke bolega.

questions.q: Find the maximum value of $n$ such that $50!$ is perfectly divisible by $12600^n$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Factorial division ke extreme cases me composite denominator ko prime factors me todna hota hai. Limit humesha badi prime number ya uski heavily loaded powers tay karti hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Prime factorization of $12600 = 2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5^2 \times 7^1$.
Powers in $50!$ nikalte hain Legendre's formula se:
Power of $7$: $\lfloor 50/7 \rfloor + \lfloor 50/49 \rfloor = 7 + 1 = 8$.
Power of $5$: $\lfloor 50/5 \rfloor + \lfloor 50/25 \rfloor = 10 + 2 = 12$. Humein groups of $5^2$ chahiye $\implies 12/2 = 6$.
Power of $3$: Limit bohot door hai (around $22/2 = 11$).
Sabse restricting factor $5^2$ ban raha hai, jo max $6$ times available hai. So max $n = 6$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Bache galti karte hain ki sirf sabse bada prime ($7$) check karte hain. Lekin yahan $5$ ki power squared thi ($5^2$), jiski wajah se uski availability aur reduce ho gayi ($12 \div 2 = 6$).

Future Exam Takeaway:
Composite divisors me sirf highest prime mat dekho. Agar chote prime ki high power demand me hai ($a^k$), toh power $k$ se divide zaroor karna!

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true? I) $\text{odd} \times \text{even} = \text{odd}$, II) $\text{odd} \times \text{odd} = \text{even}$
o: Both I and II are true
Neither I nor II is true
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Statements padh ke direct numbers put karo dimaag me. Algebraic proof ki zarurat nahi hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Check I) $\text{odd} \times \text{even}$. Take $3 \times 2 = 6$ (Even). Statement says odd. False.
Check II) $\text{odd} \times \text{odd}$. Take $3 \times 3 = 9$ (Odd). Statement says even. False.
Dono statements completely wrong hain.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Even number behaves like a black hole in multiplication; koi bhi number even se multiply hoga toh overall even hi ban jayega. Odd tabhi aata hai jab sirf odd numbers multiply ho rahe hon.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Theoretical statements me variables ke saath mat khelo. Simple prime numbers ($2, 3$) put karke seconds me counter-example dhoondh liya karo.

questions.q: Find the least number which is completely divisible by $9, 24$ and $36$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
'Least number completely divisible' matlab sedha-sedha LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) pucha hai. Language ghumaai hai bas.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Numbers hain $9, 24, 36$.
Notice karo ki $36$ exactly $9$ se divide hota hai. Toh $9$ ko picture se hi hata do.
Ab sirf $24$ aur $36$ ka LCM nikalna hai.
Highest common factor of $24, 36$ is $12$.
LCM = $12 \times (2 \times 3) = 72$. Option dekhte hi mark karo!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Jab given set of numbers me koi chota number kisi bade number ka factor ho, toh chote number ka LCM par koi effect nahi padta.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Don't draw lines and solve for LCM blindly. Eliminate factors immediately to shrink your calculation.

questions.q: Find the smallest integer which should be added to the given expression to make it a perfect square? $79998 \times 79999$
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dekhte hi algebraic identity $n(n+1)$ dikhni chahiye. Multiply karne ka paap nahi karna hai!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Let $n = 79998$. Expression is $n \times (n+1) = n^2 + n$.
Isme kya add karein ki agla perfect square $(n+1)^2$ ban jaye?
$(n+1)^2 = n^2 + 2n + 1$.
Hamare paas $(n^2 + n)$ hai, toh humein $(n + 1)$ aur chahiye.
Matlab $79998 + 1 = 79999$ add karna padega!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
General rule: Product of two consecutive integers $n(n+1)$. Add the larger number $(n+1)$ to make it $(n+1)^2$. Subtract the smaller number $n$ to make it $n^2$.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Seedha formula yaad rakh: $A \times (A+1)$ me BADA number add karne pe perfect square banta hai, aur CHHOTA number subtract karne pe.

questions.q: How many composite factors does the number $2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5^1$ have?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Total factors nikal ke Primes aur '$1$' ko hata dena hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Formula: Composite = Total Factors - Prime Factors - 1.
Total = $(3+1)(2+1)(1+1) = 4 \times 3 \times 2 = 24$.
Prime bases are $2, 3, 5$ (Total $3$ primes).
Composite = $24 - 3 - 1 = 20$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Every factor is either Prime, Composite, or Neither (which is $1$). Isiliye humesha $1$ subtract karna mat bhulna, ye CDS ka classic trap hai!

Future Exam Takeaway:
Keep this equation tattooed in memory: Total Factors = Prime + Composite + 1.

questions.q: What is the unit digit of $232^{123^{321}}$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Unit digit nikalni hai, base ka last digit $2$ hai. Yani cyclicity $4$ check hogi. Power of power ladder me trick lagao.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Power hai $123^{321}$. Ise $4$ se mod karo.
$123 \pmod 4 \equiv 3 \equiv -1$.
Reduced effective power $= (-1)^{321}$. Since power is Odd, it stays $-1$.
Math me $-1$ mod $4$ ka actual remainder hota hai: $4 - 1 = 3$.
Base unit $2^3 = 8$. Bam!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Negative remainders cyclicity calculations ke Brahmastra hote hain. Jab base cyclicity-divisor ke close ho (jaise $123 = 124 - 1$), $-1$ assume karne se power odd-even logic se ek second me tut jati hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
For any $X^{Y^Z}$ unit digit question, immediately apply modulo $4$ on base $X$'s power ladder using $+1$ or $-1$ deviation.

questions.q: Find the unit digit of $\frac{12^{55}}{3^{11}} + \frac{8^{48}}{16^{18}}$
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Never find unit digits before simplifying fractions! Denominators must be completely canceled out.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Term 1: $\frac{12^{55}}{3^{11}} = \frac{4^{55} \times 3^{55}}{3^{11}} = 4^{55} \times 3^{44}$.
Unit digit: $4^{\text{odd}} \implies 4$. $3^{44}$ (power is multiple of $4$) $\implies 1$. $4 \times 1 = 4$.
Term 2: $\frac{8^{48}}{16^{18}} = \frac{(2^3)^{48}}{(2^4)^{18}} = \frac{2^{144}}{2^{72}} = 2^{72}$.
Unit digit: $2^{72}$ (multiple of $4$) $\implies 6$.
Total Unit Digit = $4 + 6 = 10 \implies 0$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Indices ka base rule use kiya: $\frac{a^m}{a^n} = a^{m-n}$. Bacha denominator me fas ke galat unit digit nikalta hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Simplification first, cyclicity second. Base same banao, powers minus karo.
